AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #20
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. How far from the plant should the bottle drip be placed? (1 mark)
   A. About 10 to 15 cm
   B. Exactly on top of the stem
   C. In the next field
   D. Two metres

2. Which statement about a three-stone fire is correct? (1 mark)
   A. It saves the most fuel
   B. It loses a lot of heat to the air
   C. It is completely smoke-free
   D. It never needs firewood

3. Why should torn gloves not be used? (1 mark)
   A. They are too clean
   B. They are too heavy
   C. They may not protect the hands
   D. They are too big

4. What word describes manure made from once-living things? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic
   B. Mineral only
   C. Organic
   D. Metal

5. How can a family get firewood without destroying forests? (1 mark)
   A. Plant trees on their own land and replace those cut
   B. Burn grass
   C. Cut trees from forests at night
   D. Cut young trees only

6. Why should we not skip breakfast? (1 mark)
   A. It is not real food
   B. It makes you tired
   C. The body needs energy and nutrients to start the day
   D. Breakfast is a waste of money

7. Which animal often picks maize cobs and bananas? (1 mark)
   A. Hen
   B. Monkey
   C. Duck
   D. Cow

8. Why should stagnant water be emptied from tins and tyres? (1 mark)
   A. It cools the compound
   B. It smells of soap
   C. It is too clean
   D. Mosquitoes lay eggs in it

9. Why should combs and towels not be shared? (1 mark)
   A. Germs and lice can spread
   B. They become dirty faster
   C. They are too big
   D. They break

10. How does manure from animals help crops? (1 mark)
   A. It gives shade
   B. It makes crops small
   C. It scares birds
   D. It supplies plant food to the soil

11. How can you tell that a plant has enough water? (1 mark)
   A. The pot is empty
   B. The soil is dust
   C. The leaves are gone
   D. The soil is damp about a finger deep

12. Which group of animals is called poultry? (1 mark)
   A. Sheep and goats
   B. Cows and bulls
   C. Chickens, ducks and turkeys
   D. Zebras and giraffes

13. What is the main job of the trunk of a tree? (1 mark)
   A. Collect rain
   B. Carry water and food between roots and leaves
   C. Make flowers
   D. Absorb sunlight

14. How should you hold the cloth if you are right-handed? (1 mark)
   A. In your teeth
   B. Above your head
   C. In the left hand while sewing with the right
   D. Under your foot

15. How is charcoal made? (1 mark)
   A. By mixing soil and water
   B. By drying maize
   C. By boiling water
   D. By burning wood slowly with little air

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Why do we dust before sweeping? (2 marks)

17. Describe how to make a simple trellis for passion fruit. (4 marks)

18. Give two reasons why we should not kill wild animals that eat crops. (2 marks)

19. A family boils beans for a long time on a big fire with the lid off. Suggest five ways to improve fuel use. (5 marks)

20. Why do we need protective foods? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #20 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — About 10 to 15 cm
   Close enough for the roots to reach the water.

2. B — It loses a lot of heat to the air
   Open fires waste heat.

3. C — They may not protect the hands
   Holes let dirt and germs in.

4. C — Organic
   Organic means it comes from plants and animals.

5. A — Plant trees on their own land and replace those cut
   Growing trees keeps a supply of wood.

6. C — The body needs energy and nutrients to start the day
   Breakfast gives energy for school.

7. B — Monkey
   Monkeys pick crops from farms near forests.

8. D — Mosquitoes lay eggs in it
   Mosquitoes spread malaria.

9. A — Germs and lice can spread
   Personal items should be for one person.

10. D — It supplies plant food to the soil
   Manure enriches the soil.

11. D — The soil is damp about a finger deep
   Feeling the soil shows if the roots have water.

12. C — Chickens, ducks and turkeys
   Poultry means birds kept for eggs and meat.

13. B — Carry water and food between roots and leaves
   The trunk is like a pipe for the plant.

14. C — In the left hand while sewing with the right
   This is the usual way.

15. D — By burning wood slowly with little air
   Charcoal is wood partly burnt in limited air.

SECTION B
----
16. (2 marks)
   Answer: Dust falls to the floor, so sweeping afterwards removes it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dust falls, 1 mark for sweeping removes.

17. (4 marks)
   Answer: Fix strong posts about 2 m tall; tie strong wires or strings between them; plant seedlings near the posts; tie the stems gently to the wires.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

18. (2 marks)
   Answer: They are part of nature and biodiversity, and they help in other ways such as pollinating and eating pests.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason.

19. (5 marks)
   Answer: Soak the beans first, cook with the lid on, use dry wood, reduce the flame after boiling starts, cut food or use an improved jiko, put out the fire after cooking.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

20. (2 marks)
   Answer: They give vitamins and minerals that fight sickness and keep the body healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fight sickness, 1 mark for vitamins or minerals.
